lines.text: A bee drinks the nectar, and carries it home inside her.
In the hive, the workers pass it mouth to mouth, and the water dries out of it.
They fan it with their wings until it is thick enough to keep, then seal the cell with wax.
That is honey. Mostly sugar, almost no water. And that is the whole trick.
Too little water for bacteria to grow in. Faintly acidic. And it makes its own peroxide.
Which is why medical grade honey is used in licensed wound dressings today.
On skin, it is a humectant. It pulls water in, and holds it there. In hair, the same. Moisture stays, so strands stay soft.
What it will not do is grow hair. No good study shows that. For wounds and for moisture, the evidence is good. For acne and eczema, it is thinner.
Soap, cleanser, lip balm, a mask. Patch test first, and skip it if bee stings or pollen set you off.
